length_semantics_verified_from_source.if_driving_frames_greater_than_length: Truncated: `pose_video = pose_video[video_frame_offset:][:length]` -- only the first `length` frames of the driving clip are used, no error.
length_semantics_verified_from_source.if_driving_frames_less_than_length: Padded by holding the last frame: `pose_video = torch.cat((pose_video,) + (pose_video[-1:],) * (length - pose_video.shape[0]), dim=0)` -- the tail is a frozen repeat of the last real frame, not new motion. No error, but the padded tail dilutes any motion measurement across the full `length`.
length_semantics_verified_from_source.conclusion: length is not hard-constrained to multiples of 4 at the WanAnimate2ToVideo node's own input-validation level despite the UI 'step=4' (that is a spinner-increment nicety) -- but see legal_wan_length_correction below for a separate, more severe constraint discovered one level deeper, inside the VAE encode itself.

legal_wan_length_correction.the_bug: WanVAE.encode() floors ANY input pixel-frame count down to the nearest 4n+1 value before encoding: `t = 1 + ((t - 1) // 4) * 4`. This runs on EVERY vae.encode() call inside WanAnimate2ToVideo.execute() -- both the placeholder canvas latent (image shaped [length,H,W,3]) and the pose_video driving-conditioning latent (also shaped [length,H,W,3] after truncate/pad). A non-4n+1 `length` therefore silently drops trailing REAL driving frames during this internal encode -- materially more severe than the already-documented truncate/pad behavior, which is intentional and harmless.
legal_wan_length_correction.affected_runs: ALL 5 runs, not just run 5 -- the flooring applies uniformly to any length value. Runs 1-4's originally-chosen length=60 is NOT itself legal (60-1=59, 59%4=3!= 0); it would floor to 57 internally, silently dropping the last 3 frames.
legal_wan_length_correction.tooling: tools/qualification/vid184/legal_length.py (smallest_legal_wan_length, trim_to_evidence_window), verified by 12 deterministic tests in tests/tools/test_vid184_legal_length.py (no GPU/network).

legal_wan_length_correction.padding_mechanism_for_the_extra_internal: The 1 (runs 1-4) or 2 (run 5) extra internal frames use the SAME already-documented official-node behavior as any other length > driving-frame-count case: WanAnimate2ToVideo.execute()'s own hold-last-frame padding (see length_semantics_verified_from_source above), not a new or different mechanism. No driving-video content is modified to manufacture the legal length -- the existing frozen evidence-window files (39f candidate / 60f full clip) are used as-is; the node's own padding supplies the extra frames needed to reach the legal length.
legal_wan_length_correction.why_not_floor_instead_of_ceil: Flooring (e.g. 37 for the 39-frame evidence window) would DISCARD 2 real evidence frames rather than pad with 2 mechanically-explained held-last-frame repeats; ceiling to the next legal length and trimming the padded tail post-decode preserves every real evidence frame untouched.

cache_off_procedure_for_run_5.why_the_exposed_widgets_cannot_do_it: Verified from comfy_extras/nodes_wan.py, class WanAnimate2Cache.define_schema(): `device` combo options are exactly ['cpu','gpu'] (no 'off'/'none'); `dtype` combo options are exactly ['default','int8','int4']. The node ALWAYS attaches a PoseBranchCache to the model when present in the graph -- there is no widget value that disables it. True cache-OFF requires removing it from the execution path.
steps: 1. Open (double-click, or right-click -> Open Subgraph/Enter) the 'Motion Transfer (Wan Animate 2)' subgraph node for the Distilled workflow.
2. Inside it, locate the node named WanAnimate2Cache (sits between the model/LoRA loader chain and the sampler; single MODEL input, single MODEL output).
3. Click to select only that node.
4. Right-click -> 'Bypass' (or select it and press Ctrl+B). It should render muted/dashed, indicating it is now a passthrough.
5. Visually confirm the MODEL connection now effectively skips it (ComfyUI auto-routes a bypassed single-in/single-out node's matching-type wire straight through).
6. Exit back to the top-level graph.
7. Leave the outer cache_device/cache_dtype widgets at their shipped defaults -- once bypassed, the node that would read them never executes, so their values are inert.

output_files_needed_per_run.both_required: The plain generated clip AND the side-by-side comparison video the graph also saves.
output_files_needed_per_run.why_both: The generated clip alone is required for the detector-based scorer (tracking.py) -- a side-by-side composite doubles the frame width and puts the driving clip's own subject in the same frame, which would corrupt the person-detector's box coordinates and could register as a false 'ghost' detection. The side-by-side is for Rob's own human-verdict-gate visual review convenience only; the scorer never reads it.
